resolution_analysis_2026_09_26.correction: The earlier statement "platform resolution is about 0.0005" is WRONG and is retracted. That measurement was the observed change produced by one particular perturbation (a training-seed shift), not the platform resolution. The correct A/B resolution for two packages scored on the same fixed 322 test rows is a PAIRED comparison whose sampling sd is about 0.0116, so the 95% minimum detectable difference is about 0.0228.
consequences: the delivered +0.0409 is 3.5 sigma and is therefore real
any single-column improvement below about 0.023 is indistinguishable from row-sampling noise on 322 rows
this explains why the V42 candidate (+0.0144 local) could not transfer and why several 0.005-0.015 candidates were unreadable
the correct strategic bar is a LARGE structural gain (>0.02), not member tweaking at the 0.005 level

feasibility_analysis_2026_09_26.family_a_conclusion: adding noise to the base tops out at +0.00123 - a noised copy can never be a better model, so it is the wrong generative model

feasibility_analysis_2026_09_26.the_real_bar: family (b) is an optimistic upper bound. The best real member has ratio 1.06 and is better on 47.5% of rows while worse on 52.5%, and that mixture yields only +0.0103 in the blend. Therefore the empirical ceiling of member blending in this pool is about +0.010, and reaching the 0.023 threshold would require a member that is either outright better than the released column (ratio < 1) or has roughly twice the complementary error structure
what_does_not_work: no member in the pool has ratio < 1 (best is 1.06 vs the released column)
nothing adds on top of the winner (leave-one-fold-out weights zero every one of six distinct members)
the four large members are near-duplicates (rho 0.979-0.998)
alternative combination operators (sibling mean/median, trimmed mean, pure median) are all worse
feasibility_analysis_2026_09_26.conclusion: the <=0.023 gap cannot be closed by member selection. Closing it requires a fundamentally better model (different features or paradigm) that beats or substantially complements the released column, and no evidence in the current corpus shows such a model is reachable.
feasibility_analysis_2026_09_26.strategic_implication: member blending on the time column is exhausted; the honest options are to stop at 96.3143, or to start a different problem class with an unknown prior

platform_determinism.statement: re-submitting the same package returned the same score (user has repeated submissions before with identical results)
platform_determinism.consequence: the platform is deterministic for a fixed package: an observed score difference between two packages is EXACT, not noisy. There is no platform-side jitter to average out.
platform_determinism.reframing: the 0.0116 paired sd is therefore NOT the platform resolution. It is the uncertainty of GENERALIZATION: how far a local gain can differ from its realization on the fixed 322-row test set. A package with a local gain of +0.01 lands anywhere around +0.01 +- 0.012 on the leaderboard; a local gain of +0.005 is a coin flip.

engineering_lesson.title: process pool + BLAS/torch thread explosion
engineering_lesson.detail: Launched with workers=16 the batch produced ZERO completions in five minutes while single-fold timing said 6-31 s. Each forked worker had inherited 16 BLAS/torch threads (ps showed 16 threads and 432% CPU per worker), so 8-16 workers meant 128-256 threads on 32 cores, load 106 and near-zero throughput. Setting OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 alone was NOT enough; adding OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=1 made 41 trials finish in ~110 s per seed.
engineering_lesson.rule: any parallel fitting batch must pin BLAS/OMP/MKL/NUMEXPR thread counts before launch
